Appearance:
 Shri Ramesh Chandra Gangare advocate for applicant.
 Shri Santosh Singh Thakur public prosecutor for State
 Order

This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 495/2023 registered at Police Station Sonkatchha District Dewas (M.P.) for offence punishable under Section (s) 363, 366, 368, 376, 212, 34 of IPC & 5L/6 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 27.09.2024.
As per the case of prosecution, the victim aged around 15 years eloped with Gulshan on 21.7.2024 from her parental home at village Dudlai.
She and Gulshan went to Pavagadh in Gujarat.
They married in a temple.
Gulshan worked as a labourer in Osis company.
Victim and Gulshan stayed in rented room of company for nine months.
Thereafter, they had a quarrel,
So, Gulshan left her and went away.
She informed the contractor Bharat Singh Yadav that Gulshan had left her alone.
Bharat Singh informed her father but her father did not respond.

So, Bharat Singh gave her shelter at his NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:32035 2 MCRC-48294-2024 home.
She got friendly with Vikas s/o Chain Singh resident of Ranayar Kala, Dewas.
She informed Bharat Singh that she desires to marry with Vikas.
She married to Vikas on 22.8.2024 at Chamunda Mata Mandir Dewas.
She resided with Vikas in a rented room in Dewas.

Initially police station Sonkatchha District Dewas registered FIR at crime Bharat Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175827447/
1 No. 495/2023 for offence punishable under Sections 363 of IPC.

sentences.text: Later prosecution for offence punishable under Sections 366, 368, 376, 212, 34 of IPC & 5L/6 of POCSO Act were added.
Applicant - Bharat Singh was arrested on 27.09.2024, he is in custody ever since.
Other accused were also arrested.
On completion of investigation, final report was submitted.
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the matter for supporting the victim.
No offence as alleged is made out against the applicant.
Victim herself has stated that applicant provided her shelter when Gulshan left her and fled away.
There is no allegation of abduction or sexual assault against the applicant.
Learned counsel further submits that the applicant is aged around 45 years.
He is a labour contractor by profession and sole bread earner of the family.
There is no likelihood of absconsion leaving his family, home and profession.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
There is no likelihood of tampering with the evidence by the applicant.
The trial would take time to complete.
Therefore, the applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:32035 3 MCRC-48294-2024
Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
